## Why

`_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` (`src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py:1906`, ending ~`:4346`) is **2,441 lines** at nesting depth 9 — **56% of the 4,361-line `engine.py`**. It is the single largest maintainability liability in the repo and the place where a correctness bug has already been caused by code placement.

History matters here. The 2026-06-01 audit found `engine.run()` at ~3,150 lines and recommended reducing it. The subsequent fix shortened `run()` to 343 lines — but the 2026-08-11 re-audit found the complexity had been **relocated into this function**, not removed. Repeating that pattern would be worse than leaving it alone.

## BLOCKED — do not start before the characterization-coverage issue lands

This issue must not begin until branch coverage of this function has been measured and raised, with committed goldens acting as the behavioural invariant. Extracting first is precisely how the earlier placement bug happened. If the coverage issue is not merged, this one is not ready.

## Scope

Reduce `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` by extracting cohesive blocks into named, testable helpers — **one block per PR**, with golden outputs byte-identical at every step.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** change behaviour. Every PR in this series must leave `tests/baseline/test_golden/*.csv` byte-identical. If a golden changes, the extraction is wrong — do not update the golden to match.
- Do **not** do it in one PR. A 2,441-line restructure in a single diff is unreviewable and unrevertable.
- Do **not** "improve" the algorithms while extracting — no reordering, no micro-optimisation, no changing numeric formulations. Pure motion only.
- Do **not** rename existing public functions or change `engine.run()`'s signature.
- Do **not** start with the hardest block. Take the most self-contained one first.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of real extraction.

## Tasks

Each task is its own PR, in order, each independently revertible:

- [ ] **Slice 1** — extract the per-period loop body into a private helper taking an explicit parameter object. This is the largest single win and defines the seam for everything after.
- [ ] **Slice 2** — extract the turnover / transaction-cost block.
- [ ] **Slice 3** — extract the weighting-selection block.
- [ ] **Slice 4** — extract the threshold/hold entry-exit decision logic.
- [ ] After each slice: re-run the scenario goldens and confirm byte-identical output; record the function's new line count in the PR description.
- [ ] After the final slice, lower the complexity budget if one exists, and update any audit note that cites the 2,441-line figure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After each PR, all baseline/golden CSVs are **byte-identical** to before.
- [ ] After each PR, the full suite passes and `black --check .` / `ruff check --select E4,E7,E9,F` are clean.
- [ ] Each PR states the function's line count before and after, so the reduction is visible and monotonic.
- [ ] Every extracted helper has at least one direct unit test that does not go through the whole engine.
- [ ] Final state: `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` is **under 500 lines** and maximum nesting depth is **≤ 6**.
- [ ] **Named test gate**: the scenario suite from the characterization issue (`tests/baseline/test_threshold_hold_scenarios.py`) plus the existing goldens, run unchanged after every slice. No new gate is invented for this issue — the whole point is that the pre-existing net must hold.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration** (once, on the first slice): during extraction, deliberately move one statement across the extracted boundary so it executes in the wrong order; confirm a golden or scenario test **fails**; revert and confirm byte-identical output. This proves the net catches placement errors — the exact failure mode this function has already suffered.

## Implementation Notes

- Extract **outward-in**: pull whole cohesive blocks to module-level private functions, passing state explicitly. Resist introducing a class or a shared mutable context object; that hides the coupling rather than removing it.
- Five `NaN`-returning exception handlers currently live inside this function (`engine.py` ~`:3517, 3599, 3719, 3812, 3847`) and are being fixed under a separate issue. Coordinate: land that fix **before** the slices that touch those regions, or expect conflicts.
- `apply_membership_windows` is called at `engine.py:1835`, just above the function — the universe-membership work touches adjacent code; sequence to avoid collisions.
- Line numbers in this issue will drift; re-derive them at implementation time.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimension 1. Recorded there as L-effort and deliberately not filed until scoped — this is that scoping.
title: Extract _run_threshold_hold_multi_periods in reviewable slices (2,441 lines = 56% of engine.py) — BLOCKED on characterization coverage

body:
## Why

`_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` in `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` is **2,441 lines** (def at `:1906`, ending ~`:4346`) with a maximum nesting depth of 9. `engine.py` is 4,361 lines total, so this **one function is 56% of the file**.

It is also the highest-risk code in the repo to change. The 2026-06-01 audit recorded a real correctness bug caused by *code placement inside this function*, and the 2026-08-11 re-audit found that the previous "shorten `engine.run()`" effort did not reduce complexity — it **relocated** it here.

Before anyone extracts anything from it, there has to be a net. This issue builds the net; the extraction is tracked separately and must not start until this lands.

There is a second, independent reason to do this: the re-audit found the baseline fixtures are **homogeneous** — they exercise the happy path and little else, which is precisely why logic bugs in this repo survive green CI. Raising branch coverage of this function has value even if the extraction never happens.

## Scope

Establish measured branch coverage of `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` and raise it with scenario variants, so any later refactor has a behavioural invariant to hold against.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** refactor, reformat, extract, or re-indent the function in this issue. **Zero production-code changes.** Any structural change here destroys the baseline it is meant to establish.
- Do **not** chase 100% branch coverage. Target the branches a refactor would plausibly disturb: the period loop, turnover/cost handling, weighting selection, the threshold/hold entry-exit logic, and the degenerate-input paths.
- Do **not** add slow end-to-end runs that materially lengthen CI. Prefer many small scenario fixtures over few large ones.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of real coverage.

## Tasks

- [ ] Measure current branch coverage of `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` specifically (e.g. `coverage run --branch -m pytest ...` then report on `multi_period/engine.py`), and record the starting number in the PR.
- [ ] Enumerate the function's decision points and identify which are currently unexercised.
- [ ] Add scenario variants to the existing baseline/golden harness (`tests/baseline/test_golden/`) covering at minimum: zero eligible managers; a single eligible manager; turnover cap binding vs not binding; non-zero vs zero transaction cost; entry threshold met but hold period not elapsed; a manager exiting mid-sample; and a rebalance period with no change.
- [ ] Commit the resulting golden CSVs so they act as the invariant for the later extraction.
- [ ] Record the final coverage number and the delta in the PR description.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Branch coverage of `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` is measured, reported, and **materially higher** than the starting number (state both).
- [ ] Each new scenario has a committed golden output.
- [ ] The full suite still passes and existing goldens are unchanged — this issue adds coverage, it does not alter behaviour.
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows **no changes** under `src/` (tests and fixtures only).
- [ ] **Named test gate**: `tests/baseline/test_threshold_hold_scenarios.py` — the new scenario suite, each case asserting against its committed golden.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration**: make a single-line semantic change inside the function (e.g. invert the turnover-cap comparison), confirm **at least one** new scenario test fails, then revert and confirm all pass. Record which scenario caught it — that is the evidence the net actually holds.

## Implementation Notes

- This is a **prerequisite**. The companion extraction issue should be blocked on this one; extracting first is how the previous placement bug happened.
- The repo already has the harness: `tests/baseline/test_golden/*.csv` with scenario-variant files such as `test_scenario_variant_golden_cost_up_.csv`, `..._turnover_cap_down_.csv`, `..._vol_target_up_.csv`. Follow that naming and generation pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- Beware the known TMP trap: golden CSVs are excluded by a global `*.csv` `.gitignore` rule and need an explicit negation (`!tests/baseline/test_golden/*.csv`) or they silently fail to commit and CI reads as cross-OS float drift.
- The deliberate-break step is the real acceptance test here. A coverage number that goes up but catches nothing is not a net.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimensions 1 and 2 (complexity relocated, not removed; fixture homogeneity).
title: Characterization coverage for _run_threshold_hold_multi_periods (prerequisite for any extraction)

body:
## Why

Five broad exception handlers in the multi-period engine convert a failure into `NaN` and continue. In ranking code this is the worst possible failure mode: the run succeeds, the output looks like a number, and the manager silently drops to the bottom (or is excluded) for a reason nobody sees.

Verified at tip `928a523c` — every `except Exception` in `src/trend_analysis/` with a `NaN` within three lines:

| Site | Line |
|---|---|
| `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` | **3517** — `z = float("nan")` |
| `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` | **3599** — `return float("nan")` |
| `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` | **3719** — `return float("nan")` |
| `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` | **3812** — `z = float("nan")` |
| `src/trend_analysis/multi_period/engine.py` | **3847** — `z = float("nan")` |

That is the complete set — out of 265 broad handlers repo-wide, exactly these five sit on the numeric/ranking path. This is a small, bounded, high-value fix, deliberately separated from the unbounded "refactor all the handlers" work.

The consequence: a genuine bug in metric computation for one manager (bad input, dimension mismatch, divide-by-zero) is indistinguishable from "this manager legitimately has no score". Green CI, plausible output, wrong selection.

## Scope

Make these five sites fail visibly or degrade explicitly, instead of silently yielding `NaN`. Only these five handlers.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** touch the other ~260 broad handlers. They are budgeted separately by the ratchet issue; widening scope here makes the change unreviewable.
- Do **not** change ranking/selection semantics for managers that legitimately have insufficient data — a genuine "not enough history" case may still be `NaN`, but it must arrive through an explicit check, not an exception handler.
- Do **not** convert these into bare `raise` if that makes a single bad manager abort an entire multi-period run — decide per site whether the right behaviour is raise, or log-and-exclude-with-reason.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of a real fix.

## Tasks

- [ ] For each of the five sites, determine which exception types can actually occur, and narrow the `except Exception` to those.
- [ ] Replace the silent `NaN` with either (a) a raise, where the condition indicates a real defect, or (b) an explicit, logged degradation that records **which manager and why**.
- [ ] Where `NaN` remains a legitimate outcome (genuinely insufficient data), reach it via an explicit precondition check *before* the computation, not via an exception handler.
- [ ] Ensure any retained log line names the manager/period so the cause is diagnosable from a run log.
- [ ] Lower the `MAX_BROAD_EXCEPT_SRC` budget constant if the ratchet issue has landed, reflecting the handlers removed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Injecting a computation failure at each of the five sites produces either a raised error or a log entry naming the manager — never a bare `NaN` with no signal.
- [ ] A manager with genuinely insufficient history still scores `NaN` (or is excluded) through an explicit check, and the existing baseline/golden outputs are unchanged.
- [ ] No change to results for the bundled demo dataset — `tests/baseline/test_golden/*.csv` remain byte-identical.
- [ ] **Named test gate**: `tests/test_engine_nan_handlers_surface_errors.py::test_metric_failure_is_visible_not_nan` — monkeypatch the metric computation used at each site to raise, then assert for each that the run either raises or emits a log record identifying the manager, and that no silent `NaN` is produced. Parametrise over the five sites.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration**: restore `except Exception: z = float("nan")` at one site, confirm `test_metric_failure_is_visible_not_nan` **fails** for that parametrisation, revert and confirm it passes. Record both outcomes in the PR description.

## Implementation Notes

- Re-derive the five line numbers at implementation time — `engine.py` is being actively modified by the legacy-removal work and the lines will move. Regenerate with:
  ```
  grep -rn -A3 'except Exception' src/trend_analysis --include='*.py' | grep 'nan'
  ```
- All five are inside `_run_threshold_hold_multi_periods` (which spans `engine.py:1906-4346`). That function is slated for characterization coverage and later extraction — **do not** attempt any restructuring here; keep the diff to the handlers themselves so it stays reviewable and does not collide with that work.
- The 2026-06-01 audit flagged "~40 broad swallow blocks in numeric or CLI paths" and this is the sharpest remaining instance of that class.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimension 1.
title: Five engine ranking handlers turn failures into NaN instead of surfacing them

body:
## Why

Broad exception handlers have grown roughly **40 → 265** with nothing detecting the drift.

Verified at tip `928a523c`:

| Area | `except Exception` / bare `except:` |
|---|---|
| `src/trend_analysis` | **202** |
| `streamlit_app` | **63** |
| total | **265** |

The 2026-06-01 audit recorded "roughly 40 broad swallow blocks". The 2026-08-11 re-audit measured 268. It is now 265 — and that small decline is incidental drift from unrelated legacy-removal work, not a deliberate reduction.

The problem is not the absolute number; it is that **nothing stops it climbing**. Each individual handler looks locally defensible, so the count ratchets upward, and in numeric code a swallowed exception converts a bug into a plausible-looking number rather than a visible failure.

A full refactor of 265 handlers is an unbounded task and should not be attempted (that is why the re-audit deliberately did not file one). A budget ratchet is the bounded, durable fix: it costs nothing to maintain, needs no judgement about any individual handler, and makes the drift structurally impossible to repeat.

## Scope

Add a test that pins the current broad-handler count as a ceiling, so the number can only go down. Counting logic only — **no handler is changed by this issue**.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** refactor, narrow, or remove any exception handler in this issue. Zero production-code changes. (The dangerous `NaN`-returning subset is handled separately.)
- Do **not** set an aspirational target below today's count — that turns the gate red immediately and it gets disabled.
- Do **not** add a linter plugin, pre-commit hook, or new dependency. A plain test is enough and cannot drift from CI.
- Do **not** count handlers that re-raise or log-and-reraise if that materially complicates the counter; a simple, stable, documented counting rule beats a clever one.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of a working gate.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `tests/test_exception_swallow_budget.py` that walks `src/trend_analysis/` and `streamlit_app/` and counts occurrences of `except Exception` and bare `except:`.
- [ ] Assert each area's count is `<=` a module-level constant seeded with today's verified numbers: `MAX_BROAD_EXCEPT_SRC = 202`, `MAX_BROAD_EXCEPT_APP = 63`.
- [ ] Prefer AST-based counting (`ast.ExceptHandler` with `type` of `None` or `Name(id="Exception")`) over regex, so comments and strings cannot skew the count. If AST proves awkward, a documented regex is acceptable — state the rule in the docstring either way.
- [ ] Make the failure message actionable: report the current count, the budget, and instruct that the budget may be **lowered** when handlers are removed but must not be raised without an explicit decision.
- [ ] Exclude the same paths CI excludes (`archives/`, `retired/`, `.venv`, `node_modules`) so the count is stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The test passes at the current tip with the seeded budgets.
- [ ] Adding one new `except Exception:` anywhere under `src/trend_analysis/` makes it fail.
- [ ] Removing a handler and lowering the constant keeps it passing (the ratchet can tighten).
- [ ] The counting rule is documented in the module docstring, so a future reader can reproduce the number by hand.
- [ ] **Named test gate**: `tests/test_exception_swallow_budget.py::test_broad_exception_budget_not_exceeded`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration**: add a throwaway `try: pass\nexcept Exception: pass` to any module under `src/trend_analysis/`, confirm `test_broad_exception_budget_not_exceeded` **fails** with a message naming the new count, then remove it and confirm it passes. Record both outcomes in the PR description.

## Implementation Notes

- Seed the constants from a fresh measurement at implementation time rather than trusting the numbers above — the legacy-removal work is still moving these files. The commands used here were:
  ```
  grep -rn 'except Exception\|except:' src/trend_analysis --include='*.py' | wc -l   # 202
  grep -rn 'except Exception\|except:' streamlit_app     --include='*.py' | wc -l   # 63
  ```
  An AST implementation will likely produce a slightly different (more accurate) number — seed with whatever the AST counter reports, not with 202/63.
- Two separate budgets (src vs app) rather than one total, so a reduction in one area cannot mask growth in the other.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimension 1. The re-audit deliberately declined to file the 265-handler refactor as a single unbounded issue; this is the bounded half of that decision.
title: Add a broad-exception budget ratchet: 265 swallow handlers with nothing detecting the drift

body:
## Why

Every analysis run from the Streamlit UI is **survivorship-biased**, because the point-in-time universe membership path is hardcoded to `None` at both UI call sites — even though the entire backend chain that consumes it already works.

Verified at tip `928a523c`:

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| Loader | `src/trend_analysis/universe.py:40` `load_universe_membership(path) -> MembershipTable` — **implemented** |
| Applier | `universe.py:78` `apply_membership_windows(frame, membership)` — **implemented** |
| Engine | `multi_period/engine.py:68` imports it; `:1835` calls `apply_membership_windows(cleaned, membership_windows)` — **wired** |
| Config | `src/trend/config_schema.py:66,92-97,254-255` threads `universe_membership_path` — **wired** |
| **UI** | `streamlit_app/components/analysis_runner.py:431` → `universe_membership_path=None` **hardcoded** | 
| **UI** | `streamlit_app/components/guardrails.py:176` → `universe_membership_path=None` **hardcoded** |

So the only missing link is the UI never offering the input. Everything downstream of it is built, tested and connected.

Why it matters: survivorship bias is the single largest credibility problem in manager backtests. Without membership windows, a manager that blew up and left the universe still contributes returns for the whole sample, and the backtest silently overstates performance. For an allocator-facing tool this is a correctness issue, not a nicety.

## Scope

Let the user supply a point-in-time membership table in the UI, and thread it to the existing `universe_membership_path` parameter at both call sites.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** modify `universe.py`, `apply_membership_windows`, or the engine's use of it. That chain works; this issue only feeds it.
- Do **not** change the config schema — `universe_membership_path` already exists in `src/trend/config_schema.py`.
- Do **not** make membership mandatory. Absent membership must keep today's behaviour exactly (full-sample, no windowing), so existing runs and goldens are unaffected.
- Do **not** build a membership editor//CRUD UI. A file input (and optionally a bundled demo membership file) is enough.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of real wiring.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a membership-table input to the Data page (file upload or path, consistent with how the CSV/sample dataset input already works).
- [ ] Store the resolved path in session state alongside the other data settings.
- [ ] Replace the hardcoded `universe_membership_path=None` at `streamlit_app/components/analysis_runner.py:431` with the value from session state (falling back to `None`).
- [ ] Do the same at `streamlit_app/components/guardrails.py:176`, so the guardrail/preview path sees the same universe the analysis will.
- [ ] Surface the effect: after a run with membership applied, show how many managers were windowed out (or the effective universe size per period), so the user can see it took effect.
- [ ] Validate the uploaded file through `load_universe_membership` and report a clear error on a malformed table rather than silently running unwindowed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no membership supplied, results are **bit-identical** to today (no behaviour change, existing goldens unaffected).
- [ ] With a membership table that removes a manager partway through the sample, that manager contributes no returns and appears in no selection after its exit date.
- [ ] A malformed membership file produces a clear error, never a silent unwindowed run.
- [ ] Both call sites (`analysis_runner.py`, `guardrails.py`) receive the same path — the preview and the run cannot disagree about the universe.

body:
## Why

Walk-forward parameter sweeps report Sharpe with **no multiple-testing correction**, which systematically overstates significance. The correction is already implemented and never called.

`src/trend_analysis/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py:74` defines:

```python
def deflated_sharpe_ratio(
    sharpe: float, n_obs: int, skew: float, kurtosis: float, n_trials: int,
    *, sharpe_variance: float | None = None,
) -> float:
    """Return PSR deflated by the expected maximum Sharpe over ``n_trials``."""
```

Verified at tip `928a523c`: the **only** references to `deflated_sharpe_ratio` anywhere in `src/` are the re-export lines `metrics/__init__.py:407` and `:429`. The identifier `n_trials` appears nowhere else in `src/` at all. There is no production caller.

Meanwhile `src/trend_analysis/walk_forward.py` is explicitly "Utility helpers for deterministic walk-forward parameter sweeps" and builds a parameter grid (`grid` field at `:43`, validated at `:102-113`, `itertools` imported at `:5`). The trial count is therefore *knowable* — it is the size of the grid product — it is simply never passed on.

Why it matters for an allocator tool: if you try 200 parameter combinations and report the best Sharpe, that maximum is inflated by selection. Deflated Sharpe is the standard haircut. Shipping the un-deflated number next to a sweep is the kind of statistical overclaim that undermines the rest of the analysis.

## Scope

Compute the trial count (and, where available, the variance of trial Sharpes) from the walk-forward sweep and pass it into `deflated_sharpe_ratio`, surfacing the deflated figure alongside the raw Sharpe.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** modify the maths in `deflated_sharpe.py`. It validates its own inputs (`n_trials < 1` raises; `sharpe_variance` must be finite and non-negative) and is not in question.
- Do **not** replace the reported Sharpe with the deflated one. Report **both** — practitioners need the raw figure too.
- Do **not** attempt a full Bailey/López de Prado backtest-overfitting suite (PBO, CSCV). Just the DSR haircut that already exists.
- Do **not** apply DSR to single-run (non-sweep) analyses where `n_trials == 1` adds nothing.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of real wiring.

## Tasks

- [ ] In the walk-forward sweep path, compute `n_trials` as the number of parameter combinations actually evaluated (the grid product from `walk_forward.py:43,102-113`).
- [ ] Collect the per-trial Sharpe values so the observed variance can be passed as `sharpe_variance` where it is more accurate than the analytic default.
- [ ] Call `deflated_sharpe_ratio(...)` for the selected/best configuration and include the result in the sweep's output structure.
- [ ] Surface it wherever sweep results are reported, labelled clearly as deflated/haircut, next to (not instead of) the raw Sharpe.
- [ ] Guard the degenerate case: `n_trials == 1` should either skip the haircut or return the undeflated PSR — do not raise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A sweep over N > 1 parameter combinations reports both a raw Sharpe and a deflated Sharpe.
- [ ] Deflated Sharpe is **strictly less than** the raw Sharpe whenever `n_trials > 1`.
- [ ] Deflated Sharpe is **monotonically non-increasing in `n_trials`** — more trials, larger haircut, all else equal.
- [ ] `n_trials == 1` does not raise and does not report a spurious haircut.
- [ ] **Named test gate**: `tests/test_deflated_sharpe_wired.py::test_dsr_decreases_with_trial_count` — hold the return series fixed, call the sweep-level DSR computation with increasing `n_trials` (e.g. 1, 10, 100, 500) and assert the sequence is non-increasing and that all values with `n_trials > 1` are strictly below the raw Sharpe.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration**: hardcode `n_trials=1` at the call site, confirm `test_dsr_decreases_with_trial_count` **fails**, revert and confirm it passes. Record both outcomes in the PR description.

## Implementation Notes

- This is a **property test, not a golden file** — monotonicity in `n_trials` is very hard to satisfy accidentally, which is exactly what makes it a good gate. Prefer it over pinning specific numeric outputs.
- `_validate_moments` inside `deflated_sharpe.py` already rejects non-finite inputs, so skew/kurtosis must be real computed moments of the return series, not placeholders.
- If the sweep currently discards per-trial results, capturing them may be the bulk of the work; `sharpe_variance=None` is a legitimate first step (the function falls back to an analytic standard error) and can be tightened later.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimension 6 ("statistical-rigor layer"). Related prior work: issue A12 in the 2026-06-01 arc proposed deflated Sharpe; the maths landed but the wiring did not.
title: Walk-forward sweeps report Sharpe with no multiple-testing haircut: deflated_sharpe_ratio has no production caller

body:
## Why

Managers can only be ranked on raw/unadjusted metrics. `src/trend_analysis/metrics/factor_attribution.py` implements OLS factor attribution (`factor_exposures`, line 9) and is exported from `metrics/__init__.py:411`, but it carries **no `@register_metric` decorator**, so it is absent from `METRIC_REGISTRY`.

Verified at tip `928a523c` — the complete registry is:

```
annual_return  information_ratio  max_drawdown  sharpe_ratio  sortino_ratio  volatility
```

No alpha. An allocator therefore cannot rank a manager universe on **benchmark-adjusted** performance, only on raw return / risk-adjusted return. That is a meaningful analytical gap for a manager-of-managers tool: a manager whose return is entirely explained by beta to a benchmark ranks identically to one generating genuine alpha.

The selection machinery already consumes arbitrary registered metrics, so this is a wiring job, not new analytics. This is the same "exists but unwired" class as the audit's headline findings.

## Scope

Register a benchmark-adjusted alpha metric in `METRIC_REGISTRY` so it is selectable wherever existing metrics are, backed by the existing `factor_attribution` implementation.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** rewrite or "improve" the OLS estimation in `factor_attribution.py`. It is tested and works; this issue only exposes it.
- Do **not** add multi-factor model selection, factor libraries, or a factor-data loader. Single benchmark/factor frame is enough.
- Do **not** change the ranking/selection algorithm itself, or the default metric weights. Alpha must be *available*, not *default*.
- Do not add a scaffold/TODO placeholder in place of a working metric.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a registered metric (suggested name `alpha`) in `src/trend_analysis/metrics/__init__.py` using the existing `@register_metric("...")` decorator pattern — copy the shape of `sharpe_ratio` at `metrics/__init__.py:220-225`.
- [ ] Back it with `factor_attribution.factor_exposures(returns, factors, add_intercept=True)`, returning the intercept (alpha) per manager. `add_intercept=True` is already the default.
- [ ] Handle the no-benchmark case explicitly: if no benchmark/factor frame is available, the metric must raise a clear error or return `NaN` per manager — decide one and document it. It must **not** silently fall back to raw return.
- [ ] Add a finite/bounds guard on the returned value (`math.isfinite`). Non-finite alpha must not propagate into ranking — this repo's recurring defect class is relational guards that let `NaN` through.
- [ ] Confirm the metric is selectable through the same path as existing metrics (config `metrics.*` weights and any UI metric picker) without further changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `"alpha"` (or the chosen name) appears in `METRIC_REGISTRY`.
- [ ] Selecting it as the ranking metric produces a different manager ordering than `annual_return` on a fixture where the two genuinely disagree.
- [ ] With no benchmark available, behaviour is the documented one (clear error or `NaN`), never a silent fallback.
- [ ] A non-finite alpha never reaches the ranking comparison.
- [ ] **Named test gate**: `tests/metrics/test_alpha_metric_registered.py::test_alpha_ranks_below_raw_return_for_pure_beta_manager` — build two managers: A with high raw return that is entirely benchmark beta (zero alpha), B with lower raw return but positive alpha. Assert A ranks **above** B under `annual_return` and **below** B under `alpha`. Also assert `"alpha" in METRIC_REGISTRY`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration**: remove the `@register_metric` decorator, confirm the test **fails**, restore it and confirm it passes. Record both outcomes in the PR description.

## Implementation Notes

- Registry decorator: `register_metric(name)` at `src/trend_analysis/metrics/__init__.py:25`; `METRIC_REGISTRY = _METRIC_REGISTRY` at line 22.
- Reference implementation shape: `@register_metric("sharpe_ratio")` at `metrics/__init__.py:220`, which takes `(returns, risk_free=0.0, periods_per_year=12)`.
- `factor_exposures(returns: pd.DataFrame, factors: pd.DataFrame, *, add_intercept: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame` (`factor_attribution.py:9`). It aligns rows by index and drops rows with any missing value before fitting, and requires at least `len(factors.columns) + 2` observations.
- The demo dataset already carries an `SPX` benchmark column, which is a natural single-factor input for the test fixture.
- Source: 2026-08-11 re-audit, dimension 6. Full context in `Code/Audits/Trend_Model_Project/2026-08-11-AUDIT_REPORT.md`.
title: Register benchmark-adjusted alpha as a selectable ranking metric (factor_attribution exists but is not in METRIC_REGISTRY)

- [ ] Update `scripts/compare_perf.py::_default_threshold` to read one documented environment variable or `.env` key, with absent, valid, and invalid cases.
- [ ] Replace exact minor tuples in `scripts/validate_llm_deps.py` with supported ranges sourced from `pyproject.toml` or one maintained compatibility table, with boundary tests.

adding fields without testing both trigger paths fails this issue.

## Why

The public CSV loader accepts a configured date-column name and canonicalizes it to `Date` before shared validation (`src/trend_analysis/data.py:395-405,435-443`). The public Parquet loader has no explicit `date_column` parameter and sends the raw frame directly to the same validator (`src/trend_analysis/data.py:476-514`). Because `load_parquet` accepts `**_legacy_kwargs` at line 483, a caller can even pass `date_column="Timestamp"` without a Python argument error; the keyword is silently ignored and validation still expects `Date`.

This is a **current public-API consistency defect**: the same market-data schema and configured timestamp field work through CSV but fail or are silently misinterpreted through Parquet. Issue #5417 correctly fixed the requested main CSV paths; this is a newly verified follow-up rather than an omission from that issue.

## Scope

Give `load_parquet` the same configured-date-column contract as `load_csv`, use the existing `_canonicalise_date_column` helper before validation, and cover both the explicit custom-column path and default `Date` path.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change CSV loading behavior or the canonical internal column name `Date`.
- Do NOT change Parquet dependency packaging or Monte Carlo bundle schemas.
- Do NOT introduce a second date-column canonicalization helper.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a signature parameter without applying `_canonicalise_date_column` before `_validate_payload`, or adding a test that only uses the default `Date` column, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add explicit `date_column: str = "Date"` to `src/trend_analysis/data.py::load_parquet`, matching `load_csv`.
- [ ] Pass the frame returned by `pd.read_parquet` through `_canonicalise_date_column(raw, date_column)` before `_validate_payload` at `src/trend_analysis/data.py:506-514`.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_date_column_parquet_path.py` with a `Timestamp`-named Parquet fixture and a default-`Date` control case.
- [ ] Add a negative test asserting a missing configured column raises `MarketDataValidationError` when `errors="raise"`, matching the CSV contract.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification in Acceptance Criteria and capture the fail/pass evidence in the PR description.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_date_column_parquet_path.py::test_load_parquet_honors_configured_date_column` writes a Parquet frame with `Timestamp`, loads it with `date_column="Timestamp"`, and receives validated output with the canonical `Date` field.
- [ ] `tests/test_date_column_parquet_path.py::test_load_parquet_default_date_column_unchanged` proves an existing `Date`-column Parquet file loads unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/test_date_column_parquet_path.py::test_load_parquet_rejects_missing_configured_date_column` asserts `MarketDataValidationError` names the missing configured column when `errors="raise"`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily bypass `_canonicalise_date_column` in `load_parquet`. `test_load_parquet_honors_configured_date_column` must FAIL with the missing-`Date` validation path. Revert the break and confirm the test passes before requesting review.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse `src/trend_analysis/data.py::_canonicalise_date_column` at lines 364-375.
- CSV reference implementation: `src/trend_analysis/data.py:395-445`.
- Parquet gap: `src/trend_analysis/data.py:476-517`.
- Existing CSV regression: `tests/test_date_column_main_path.py`.
- The test environment needs the declared Parquet engine; issue #5347 previously made `pyarrow` explicit.
- Confirmed-green baseline before this issue: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_date_column_main_path.py tests/test_data.py`.

body:
## Why

Volatility-regime classification intentionally scales the calculated volatility, configured threshold, and neutral band together when `annualise_volatility` is enabled (`src/trend_analysis/regimes.py:218-232`). `tests/test_regime_annualise.py` pins the resulting contract: toggling annualization alone must not change regime labels. In other words, the configured boundary remains on one effective per-period basis and the implementation converts all compared values together.

The User Guide instead states that “the threshold is interpreted as annualised volatility when `annualise_volatility: true`” (`docs/UserGuide.md:305-307`). That wording tells users to provide an annualized threshold, which the implementation will multiply by `sqrt(periods_per_year)` again. This is a **current documentation-contract defect** that can produce materially incorrect regime classification even though the underlying code and regression test are coherent.

## Scope

Correct the documented units and examples for volatility-mode `regime.threshold` and `regime.neutral_band`, and add a documentation contract test that prevents the annualized-input interpretation from returning.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the classification behavior implemented for issue #5396.
- Do NOT change rolling-return regime semantics.
- Do NOT add a new regime model or configuration field.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: changing one sentence while examples or configuration comments still instruct users to pre-annualize the threshold is a failure of this issue. The verification gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `docs/UserGuide.md:280-307` to state the input basis for volatility-mode `regime.threshold` and `regime.neutral_band`, and explain that code rescales them with the signal to preserve classification when display annualization changes.
- [ ] Review the comments for `regime.threshold`, `regime.neutral_band`, and `regime.annualise_volatility` in `config/defaults.yml`, `config/demo.yml`, and `config/trend.toml`; update any comment that implies callers should pre-annualize the boundary.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_regime_documentation_contract.py` asserting the canonical User Guide wording and referenced configuration example describe classification invariance and do not instruct users to supply an already annualized threshold.
- [ ] Link the explanation to the existing behavioral regression in `tests/test_regime_annualise.py` rather than duplicating its numerical logic in documentation tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_regime_documentation_contract.py::test_user_guide_matches_regime_annualisation_contract` passes and checks that `docs/UserGuide.md` describes threshold/band rescaling alongside volatility and classification invariance.
- [ ] `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_regime_annualise.py tests/test_regime_documentation_contract.py` passes, showing documentation and behavior agree.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily restore the current sentence from `docs/UserGuide.md:305-307` that tells users the supplied threshold is interpreted as annualized volatility. `test_user_guide_matches_regime_annualisation_contract` must FAIL. Revert the sentence and confirm the test passes before requesting review.

## Implementation Notes

- Behavioral implementation: `src/trend_analysis/regimes.py:218-232`.
- Existing behavior gate: `tests/test_regime_annualise.py`.
- Contradictory documentation: `docs/UserGuide.md:305-307`.
- This is a documentation correction following issue #5396 / PR #5449; the implementation should remain classification-invariant.

body:
## Why

The runtime signal parser in `src/trend_analysis/pipeline_helpers.py:391-469` accepts legacy aliases, falls back to global `vol_adjust`, preserves a positive numeric `signals.zscore` value, and may return `None` so the pipeline derives the signal window. The independently maintained report/run-spec parser in `src/trend_model/spec.py:159-177` does not implement those semantics and converts every nonzero `signals.zscore` value to boolean `True` at line 176.

The portfolio result already records the effective runtime object as `details["signal_spec"]` (`src/trend_analysis/stages/portfolio.py:860-861`), but unified reporting resolves parameters from `config._trend_run_spec` or `config.trend_spec` (`src/trend/reporting/unified.py:487-494`). A run configured with `signals.zscore: 2.0` can therefore compute with numeric scale `2.0` while its report summarizes the separately parsed boolean form. This is a **current audit-metadata defect**: exported parameters can describe a different signal specification from the one used to calculate results.

## Scope

Create one canonical mapping-to-`TrendSpec` conversion for shared signal fields and ensure unified reports prefer the effective runtime `signal_spec` carried by the result. Preserve caller-specific behavior only as explicit wrappers, such as “no signals section means derive the runtime window.”

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT retire `trend_model` or remove compatibility entry points as part of this issue.
- Do NOT change `TrendSpec` signal mathematics or reinterpret existing numeric z-score configuration.
- Do NOT mechanically merge unrelated backtest-spec construction.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: extracting a helper while reports can still summarize a different `TrendSpec` than `result.details["signal_spec"]` is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks
